answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybils is graduated trust. A new identity starts in a hollow position with zero privileges, and earns standing only by completing real work over time, like a quill that fills a ledger one honest entry at a time. Every action is signed, priced and published, so a safe harbor of verifiable history grows around identities that behave well. Faking a thousand histories costs far more than one identity is worth, which makes mass fake accounts a losing trade.
